title: An integral reduced affine cover with quasi-compact generic points
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. There exist a reduced affine scheme $C$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and a surjective integral morphism $p:C\to Y$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] such that the set $C_{\mathrm{gen}}$ of generic points of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $C$, with the subspace Zariski topology, is quasi-compact: every cover of this subspace by open subsets has a finite subcover. The scheme $Y$ need not be reduced or Noetherian; the empty scheme is allowed.

source.place: Definition (3.8), Properties (3.9)(iii),(vi), printed pp.13-14, and the first two sentences of the affine case in the proof of Theorem (3.10), printed p.14 Read online at the source URL; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$. For each prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ let $K_{\mathfrak p}=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $u_{\mathfrak p}:A\to K_{\mathfrak p}$ be the canonical residue map. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field] says that $K_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field and $\ker u_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p$. Form the set-indexed product ring $P=\prod_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A}K_{\mathfrak p}$ and the ring map $u=(u_{\mathfrak p})$. Define $B$ to be the set of elements of $P$ integral over $A$ via $u$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] this is a subring containing $u(A)$. Thus $u$ factors as $A\xrightarrow{v}B\hookrightarrow P$, and every $b\in B$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$. Set $C=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $p=\operatorname{Spec}v$ using [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. No injectivity of $u$ or reducedness of $A$ is asserted.

source.place: Agent construction for Theorem (3.10), affine-case compact-generics reduction; compare Properties (3.9)(vi). Integral-elements subring: Stacks algebra.tex, Tag 00GO, lemma-integral-closure-is-ring.

proof.text: The ring $B$ is reduced: if $b^n=0$, every coordinate of $b$ in the product of fields $P$ is zero, hence $b=0$. To verify that $C$ is reduced as a scheme, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c), applied to the whole affine open $C$, identifies each local ring with $B_{\mathfrak q}$. If $(b/s)^n=0$ there, choose $t\notin\mathfrak q$ with $tb^n=0$. Then $(tb)^n=t^{n-1}(tb^n)=0$ in $B$, so $tb=0$ and $b/s=0$. Thus all these local rings are reduced, which is exactly [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. This is the explicit localization argument in Stacks Tag 01J2, lemma-affine-reduced.

source.place: Tag 01J2, lemma-affine-reduced, with the localization calculation written out; Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6), for the affine stalk.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integral-affine-cover-criterion] to the one-member affine covering $\{Y\}$ of $Y$. Its inverse image is the affine scheme $C$, and its map on global sections is $v:A\to B$ by the spectrum construction of [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The defining monic equations for $B$ in step 1 give exactly the ring-integrality hypothesis. Consequently $p:C\to Y$ is integral. The criterion assumes no finiteness of $A$ or of the product indexing set.

source.place: Tag 02K8, lemma-integral-local, equivalence (1) and (2), specialized to the whole affine target.

proof.text: For every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, restrict the coordinate projection $P\to K_{\mathfrak p}$ to a homomorphism $w_{\mathfrak p}:B\to K_{\mathfrak p}$. Its composite with $v$ is $u_{\mathfrak p}$. By clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field], $\operatorname{Spec}(w_{\mathfrak p})$ sends the point of $\operatorname{Spec}K_{\mathfrak p}$ to a point of $C$, and $\operatorname{Spec}(u_{\mathfrak p})$ sends it to $\ker u_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p$ in $Y$. Contravariant functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $p\circ\operatorname{Spec}(w_{\mathfrak p})=\operatorname{Spec}(u_{\mathfrak p})$. Hence every point of $Y$ has a preimage, proving surjectivity. This also shows why nilpotents in $A$ cause no difficulty.

source.place: Tag 01J5, section Points of schemes, discussion before Tag 01J9, lemma-characterize-points; algebra.tex, discussion following Tag 00CT, residue map at a prime.

proof.text: For $b\in B$ define an element $e_b\in P$ coordinatewise: its $\mathfrak p$-coordinate is $1$ when $b_{\mathfrak p}=0$ and $0$ otherwise. It satisfies $e_b^2=e_b$ and hence the monic equation $T^2-T=0$ over the image of $A$. The definition [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] therefore places $e_b$ in $B$. Coordinatewise $be_b=0$. If $bc=0$ with $c\in B$, then $c_{\mathfrak p}=0$ whenever $b_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$, since $K_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field. Therefore $c=e_bc$. Conversely every multiple of $e_b$ annihilates $b$. We have proved $\{c\in B:bc=0\}=e_bB$ by an explicit coordinate calculation, without assuming that the whole product $P$ is integral over $A$.

source.place: Agent coordinate proof for the weaker ring needed here; compare the idempotent-annihilator observation after Proposition 5, p.776, and the product-of-fields construction in section 1, pp.768-769.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-idempotent-annihilator-generic-retraction] to $B$, whose reducedness was proved in step 2 and whose principal annihilators were computed in step 5. It gives a continuous retraction $r:C\to C_{\mathrm{gen}}$ onto exactly the generic points of the irreducible components, with their subspace topology. The affine scheme $C$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Given an open cover of $C_{\mathrm{gen}}$, its inverse images under $r$ form an open cover of $C$, so finitely many suffice. Since $r$ is the identity on $C_{\mathrm{gen}}$, the corresponding original opens cover $C_{\mathrm{gen}}$. This is the required quasi-compactness. If $Y$ is empty, the product $P$ over its empty prime set and its subring $B$ are the zero ring, so $C$ and its generic-point space are empty and all assertions remain valid.

source.place: Agent assembly of the compact-generics reduction in Theorem (3.10), compare Property (3.9)(iii); quasi-compactness of spectra: Stacks algebra.tex, Tag 00E8, lemma-quasi-compact.

Step 1: P is the product of the residue fields κ(p); spec-field-point-residue-field(1) gives kernel p; B is the integral closure (def-weil-pbc-integral-closure gives a subring containing u(A)). Step 2: B lies in a product of fields, so it is reduced; its stalks are B_q by affine-open-stalk-localization(c), and (b/s)^n=0 gives t b^n=0, so tb=0; matches Stacks 01J2. Step 3: integral-affine-cover-criterion applied to the single cover {Y}. Step 4: the projections w_p and clause (3) send the point to ker u_p=p, so p is surjective. Step 5: the indicator e_b solves T^2-T, so it lies in B, and Ann(b)=e_bB is a coordinate check. Step 6: the retraction plus quasi-compactness of affine C (affine-scheme-qcqs) give quasi-compact C_gen; the empty case also holds. Tested on the zero ring, a domain, an infinite product of fields, and k[x,y]/(xy), which the hypothesis rightly excludes.
